title: Why the Winter Solstice Happens
description:
The winter solstice marks the shortest day and longest night in the Northern Hemisphere, while the Southern Hemisphere celebrates the beginning of summer. But what really causes this astronomical event? In this video, we explain the Earth’s axial tilt of 23.5°, how the solstice works, and why it’s not about distance from the sun but the angle at which sunlight hits the Earth.

From ancient monuments like Stonehenge in England and Machu Picchu in Peru that tracked the sun’s movements, to modern space-based understanding of Earth’s orbit, we uncover the science of the solstice. We look at why the sun stands directly above the Tropic of Capricorn, why the Northern Hemisphere leans away while the Southern Hemisphere leans toward the sun, and why after December 21st, days begin to grow longer again in the north.

If you’ve searched for “winter solstice explained,” “shortest day of the year,” “science of solstice,” “why seasons happen,” or “Tropic of Capricorn sun position” this video gives you the rational perspective. Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share…
